input.question: If HIV is a retro virus, why can't we find a way to stop reverse transcriptase from working?
input.ground_truth: We do! [Reverse-transcriptase inhibitors](_URL_0_) are a class of anti-retroviral drugs that operate as you suggest. But we tend to see the same problem in highly targeted drugs acting on a disease that mutates easily (like HIV or cancer). The disease gains resistance to the drug by acquiring slight changes in the shape of the target protein.

Question: If HIV is a retro virus, why can't we find a way to stop reverse transcriptase from working?

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine you have a little toy box (that’s your body), and a sneaky little robot (that’s the HIV virus). This robot is special because it has a magic copying machine inside called “reverse transcriptase.” 

Normally, when you want to build something, you use a plan (like a drawing) to make it real. But this sneaky robot does it backwards! It makes a drawing *from* the thing it built, instead of building from the drawing. That’s what “reverse transcriptase” does—it helps the virus make a drawing (its genes) from the thing it made first (which is usually not how things work in your body).

Now, scientists thought, “Hey! If we can break the copying machine (stop reverse transcriptase), the robot can’t make more sneaky robots!” So, they made special medicines called “drugs” that try to stop the copying machine from working.

But here’s why it’s tricky:
- The copying machine is hidden inside the sneaky robot.
- The robot changes its copying machine a little bit every time it makes a new copy, so the medicine sometimes doesn’t fit anymore.
- The robot hides really well in your body.

So, even though we know how to stop the copying machine, the sneaky robot keeps changing it, and hides so well, that it’s hard for the medicine to always catch it. That’s why it’s really hard to completely stop the virus with just one way of blocking reverse transcriptase.

But scientists keep trying to make better medicines and tricks to catch the sneaky robot!
